**Plan:**

The blocking dependence is a loop-carried RAW on array `v`: iterations write `v[jv[i]]` and later iterations read `v[kv[i]]`. When `jv[i] == kv[j]` for `i < j`, iteration `j` depends on iteration `i` through the value written to `v`.

The fix is to split the single loop into two sequential passes:
1. **First pass:** reads from `v` and writes to `u` (line 6 only) — no writes to `v`, so the RAW source is removed
2. **Second pass:** reads from `u` (now complete and stable) and writes to `v` (line 7 only) — no loop-carried reads of `v`

This preserves semantics because the original code's data dependence is that `u` updates depend on `v`, and `v` updates depend on `u`. By computing all `u` updates first, then all `v` updates, we respect this order without value flowing between iterations of the same loop.

DiscoPoP will now be able to detect a Do-All or Reduction pattern in each of the two loops independently, since the blocking RAW on `v` is gone from both.Done. The loop has been split into two sequential passes to eliminate the loop-carried RAW dependence on `v`. The first pass computes all updates to `u`, and the second pass computes all updates to `v` based on the completed `u` values. This maintains the original semantics while breaking the value flow between iterations that was blocking parallelization.
